title:
A study to investigate the effect of mitapivat on transfusion
burden in subjects with sickle cell disease
official: A Phase 3, Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter Study to Evaluate the Effect of Mitapivat on Transfusion Burden in Subjects With Sickle Cell Disease
summary:
Main objective: To determine the effect of mitapivat versus placebo on the need for transfusions in
subjects with SCD
conditions: Anemia in subjects with sickle cell disease (SCD)
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Age ≥12 years.
2. 2. Documented diagnosis of SCD (HbSS, HbSC, HbS/β0-thalassemia, HbS/β+-thalassemia, or other sickle cell syndrome variants).
3. 3. No more than 10 SCPCs in the 12 months before providing informed assent/consent.
4. 4. At least 1 transfusion of packed RBCs in the 12 months before informed assent/consent.
5. 5. Hb ≥5.5 and ≤10.5 g/dL. Hb concentration must be based on an average of at least 2 Hb concentration measurements (separated by ≥7 days) collected during the Screening Period.
6. 6. Additional signs or symptoms of hemolysis, as evidenced by any laboratory assessment during the Screening Period with a. Hb <8 g/dL, or b. Absolute reticulocyte count >ULN, or c. Indirect bilirubin >ULN, or d. LDH >ULN
7. 7. If taking hydroxyurea, the hydroxyurea dose must be stable for at least 90 days prior to randomization. Discontinuation of hydroxyurea requires a 90-day washout prior to informed assent/consent.
8. 8. WOCBP and pediatric female subjects who have attained menarche must be abstinent of sexual activities that may induce pregnancy as part of their usual lifestyle or agree to use a highly effective method of contraception from the time of providing informed assent/consent, throughout the study, and for 28 days after the last dose of study drug; if the highly effective method of contraception is hormonal contraception, then an acceptable barrier method must also be used.
9. 9. Written informed assent/consent (for subjects under 18 years of age, or prior to the age at which a subject is considered legally an adult per local regulations, parental permission and child assent will be obtained) must be obtained before any study-related procedures are conducted and subjects must be willing to comply with all study procedures for the duration of the study.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Pregnant, breastfeeding, or parturient.
2. 19. Known allergy to mitapivat or tablet excipients (microcrystalline cellulose, croscarmellose sodium, sodium stearyl fumarate, mannitol, magnesium stearate, and the Opadry Blue II film-coat [hypromellose, titanium dioxide, lactose monohydrate, triacetin, and FD&C Blue #2]).
3. 20. Any medical, hematological, psychological, or behavioral condition(s), including alcohol use disorder, or prior or current therapy that, in the opinion of the Investigator, may confer an unacceptable risk to participating in the study and/or could confound the interpretation of the study data.
4. 2. Receiving regularly scheduled RBC transfusion therapy (also termed chronic, prophylactic, or preventative transfusion); episodic transfusion in response to worsened anemia or VOC is permitted. Additionally, a subject who requires episodic transfusion(s) may not have received a transfusion within 60 days before providing informed assent/consent or during the Screening Period.
5. 21. Receiving herbal or dietary supplements that have not been stable in dose and preparation for ≥8 weeks prior to randomization.
6. 3. Hospitalized for an SCPC and/or other vaso-occlusive event within 14 days prior to providing informed assent/consent or during the Screening Period. A hospitalization is defined as an in-patient admission to a hospital that may or may not be preceded by an emergency room or outpatient clinic visit. A visit to an emergency room that does not result in an in-patient admission does not meet the definition of hospitalization.
7. 4. Currently receiving treatment with a disease-modifying therapy for SCD (eg, voxelotor, crizanlizumab, L-glutamine), with the exception of hydroxyurea. The last dose of voxelotor, crizanlizumab, and L-glutamine must have been administered at least 90 days before randomization.
8. 5. History of any malignancy except for nonmelanomatous skin cancer in situ, cervical carcinoma in situ, or breast carcinoma in situ. Subjects must not have active disease or received anticancer treatment ≤5 years before providing informed assent/consent.
9. 6. History of active and uncontrolled cardiac or pulmonary disease within 6 months before randomization
10. 8. Renal dysfunction as defined by an estimated glomerular filtration rate <30 mL/min/1.73 m2 by the Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration creatinine equation.
11. 9. Active uncontrolled infection requiring systemic antimicrobial therapy.
12. 11. Positive test for HIV-1 antibody or HIV-2 antibody.
13. 10. Positive test for HCV Ab with evidence of active HCV infection, or positive test for HBsAg.
14. 7. Hepatobiliary disorders
15. 12. History of major surgery (including splenectomy) ≤16 weeks before providing informed assent/consent and/or planning on undergoing a major surgical procedure during the study.
16. 13. Current enrollment or past participation (within 90 days before randomization or a time frame equivalent to 5 half-lives of the investigational study drug, whichever is longer) in any other clinical study involving an investigational study drug or device.
17. 14. Past enrollment in a clinical study involving mitapivat.
18. 15. Prior exposure to gene therapy or prior bone marrow or stem cell transplantation.
19. 16. Currently receiving treatment with hematopoietic stimulating agents; the last dose must have been administered at least 90 days before randomization.
20. 17. Receiving products that are strong inhibitors of CYP3A4/5 that have not been stopped for ≥5 days or a time frame equivalent to 5 half-lives (whichever is longer), or strong inducers of CYP3A4 that have not been stopped for ≥28 days or a time frame equivalent to 5 half-lives (whichever is longer), prior to randomization.
21. 18. Receiving anabolic steroids that have not been stopped for at least 4 weeks before randomization. Testosterone replacement therapy to treat hypogonadism is allowed; the testosterone dose and preparation must be stable for ≥10 weeks before randomization.
